steps.title: Synchronize worms by staging embryos
steps.instruction: Create synchronized L4 populations over four days by moving 20 young adult worms per plate at specified times.

substeps.instruction: Day 1, 9:00 am: Using a worm pick, transfer 20 young adult worms onto a fresh NGM plate seeded with OP50; repeat to make three plates (≈10 min total).
Day 1, 5:00 pm: Transfer the same 20 worms from each of the three plates onto new OP50‑seeded NGM plates (three new plates).
Days 2–3, each morning (9:00 am) and evening (5:00 pm): Transfer 20 adult worms from each existing plate onto fresh OP50‑seeded NGM plates, creating three new plates each time.
After the evening transfer on Day 3, move the original adult worms to fresh plates both morning and evening for one additional day.

steps.title: Label SNAP and HALO tags
steps.instruction: Stain synchronized L4s with a 1 mM JF646‑HALO / JF549‑SNAP dye mixture to a final 25 µM concentration, then recover on OP50 plates in the dark.

substeps.instruction: Inspect Day 4 evening plates; select those with abundant L4 hermaphrodites.
Wash worms off the three selected plates with ~1 mL M9 buffer using a glass Pasteur pipette; collect in a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge briefly (≈10 s) on a benchtop centrifuge, discard supernatant, and wash three times with 1 mL M9 buffer.
Resuspend the washed worms in ~195 µL M9 buffer.
Prepare dye mixture: dissolve each JF dye (JF646‑HALOtag and JF549‑cp‑SNAPtag) to 1 mM in DMSO (e.g., 5 nmol in 5 µL DMSO). Combine the two 5 µL aliquots to obtain 5 µL of a 1 mM 1:1 dye mixture.
Add the 5 µL dye/DMSO mixture to the worm suspension to reach a final dye concentration of 25 µM (ensure DMSO stays ≤5%).
Vortex gently to mix, then place the tube (lid on) in a freezer box on an orbital shaker at room temperature for 120 min.
Every 15 min, flick the tube and briefly spin down worms to prevent clumping; keep the tube protected from light.
After 2 h, spin down, aspirate supernatant, and wash worms four times with 1 mL M9 buffer.
Using a Pasteur pipette, transfer the washed worms onto at least three OP50‑seeded NGM plates; allow the M9 droplet to dry completely (perform in a dark drawer).
Once dry, cap the plates, invert them, and let the worms recover in a lidded freezer box for 10–12 h in darkness (preferably allowing the L4→adult molt).

steps.title: Prepare agarose imaging pad
steps.instruction: Make a 4 % agarose pad, add 25 mM NaN₃, and mount 20 young adult worms for imaging.

substeps.instruction: Heat a 4 % agarose aliquot in a 95 °C heat block until dissolved.
Place a small drop of molten agarose on a microscope slide and flatten with a second slide to form a pad.
Trim the solidified pad to ~10 mm × 5 mm so it fits entirely under a coverslip.
Add 2–4 µL of 25 mM sodium azide (NaN₃) onto the pad; spread evenly with a worm pick (reduce volume if it spreads off the pad).
Transfer 20 young adult worms onto the NaN₃‑treated pad.
Allow worms to paralyze and straighten (a few minutes). If the NaN₃ droplet begins to dry, place the slide in a humidity chamber.
Seal the pad with a Zeiss 1.5 high‑performance coverslip, then seal the coverslip edges with nail polish.
Proceed to imaging promptly (do not exceed 60 min total exposure to NaN₃).

steps.title: Set up 3‑color super‑resolution imaging
steps.instruction: Configure the microscope for 3‑color imaging and acquire low‑power pre‑focus frames.

substeps.instruction: Arrange laser lines in descending wavelength order: 1) 646 nm, 2) 549 nm, 3) 488 nm.
In widefield mode, locate worms on the pad and coverslip.
Switch to super‑resolution mode and set laser power to <1 % of maximum.
Set exposure time to 300 ms.
Focus both imaging planes on the dorsal nerve cord as tightly as possible.
Turn lasers off immediately after focusing; keep the laser on for <10 s while finding the cord.
After the cord is in focus, reduce exposure time to 30 ms and begin recording.
Adjust laser powers to achieve optimal blinking while preserving fluorophore lifespan (refer to Figure 3B for an example).

steps.title: Acquire images for channel counting
steps.instruction: Collect super‑resolution data suitable for counting individual calcium‑channel emitters.

substeps.instruction: Organize laser lines by target protein first, then fiducial markers.
In widefield mode locate worms; switch to super‑resolution mode.
Use laser power <1 % and exposure 300 ms to focus on the dorsal nerve cord.
After focusing, increase laser power to 4–12 % (with a 200 mW laser and 40 µm biplane module) to induce blinking.
Record until the dyes are fully bleached (typically ~4,000 frames).
Ensure the sample is not exposed to light outside the imaging box.

steps.title: Perform localization analysis
steps.instruction: Process raw image stacks to extract precise fluorophore localizations.

substeps.instruction: Open the Localization tab in the analysis software.
Set the background threshold between 3 and 5 (optimal for C. elegans).
Adjust the threshold to minimize background cutouts while retaining real signals.
Use the ROI‑frame (Probe x) slider to select frames that show blinking; move 10 frames forward and backward (≈600 ms range) to verify on/off behavior.
Exclude frames without blinking from further analysis.

steps.title: Visualize and export localization data
steps.instruction: Filter, denoise, and save reconstructed images and particle lists for downstream quantification.

substeps.instruction: Open the Visualization tab.
Discard localizations with radial precision >50 nm; display remaining points as 50 nm particles.
Denoise using Method: “Mean Distance” and “Denoise by Percent”; lower the slider until signal outside the dorsal cord is removed while the cord signal remains intact.
Save the denoised image in the View Manager.
For each synaptic bouton, draw a circular ROI of 700 nm radius centered on an in‑focus dense projection and save the view.
Export the ROI data as a particle .csv file.
Analyze five synapses per animal from five different animals (total 25 synapses). Name files as “animal#_synapse#.csv”.

steps.title: Cluster analysis of channel localizations
steps.instruction: Group localizations into putative calcium‑channel clusters and export the results.

substeps.instruction: Open the Advanced Statistics dialogue and select the Cluster Analysis tab.
Set Maximum particle distance to 60 nm (≈size of a calcium channel plus localization error).
Set Minimum particle count per cluster to 2.
Click Compute to generate clusters.
Export the cluster table as a .csv file.
